questions.question: In a displacement reaction, what is the key factor that determines whether a more reactive metal will displace a less reactive metal from its compound?

options.text: Position of the metals in the reactivity series

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Position of the metals in the reactivity series**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **displacement reaction**, the reactivity of the metals involved plays a crucial role.
 
• The **reactivity series** is an arrangement of metals in order of their reactivity, from most reactive to least reactive.
 
• A more reactive metal can displace a less reactive metal from its compound.
 
• This is because the more reactive metal has a greater tendency to lose electrons and form positive ions.
 
• For example, **zinc** can displace **copper** from copper sulfate solution because zinc is higher in the reactivity series than copper.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Temperature of the reaction**__

 __
 
• While **temperature** can affect the rate of reaction, it does not determine whether one metal will displace another.
 
• Displacement reactions are more influenced by the reactivity of the metals involved.
 
 
 
• **Size of the metal atoms**__
 __
 
• The **size of metal atoms** does not play a significant role in displacement reactions.
 
• It is the reactivity and ability to lose electrons that matter more in these reactions.
 
 
 
• **Concentration of the compound**__
 
 
• While the **concentration** of the compound can affect the rate of a reaction, it does not determine the displacement of metals.
 
• The ability to displace another metal is primarily dependent on the relative reactivity of the metals.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about solutions is correct?

options.text: Solutions can be separated using simple filtration.
The solute is present in a smaller amount than the solvent.
The concentration of a solution can only be expressed in terms of mass per cent.
A solution is a heterogeneous mixture.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The solute is present in a smaller amount than the solvent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **solution** is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances.
 
• In a solution, the substance in the **smaller amount** is called the **solute** and the substance in the **larger amount** is called the **solvent**.
 
• The **solute** dissolves in the **solvent** to form a solution.
 
• For example, in a saltwater solution, **salt** is the **solute** and **water** is the **solvent**.
 
• It is possible to have solutions where the solute is present in a very small amount compared to the solvent, such as in dilute solutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Simple Filtration**__

 __
 
• **Simple filtration** is a method used to separate an **insoluble solid** from a liquid.
 
• **Solutions** cannot be separated by simple filtration because the **solute** is completely dissolved in the **solvent**.
 
 
 
• **Concentration of a Solution**__
 __
 
• The **concentration** of a solution can be expressed in various ways, such as **mass per cent, molarity, molality**, and **normality**.
 
 
 
• **Heterogeneous Mixture**__
 
 
• A **heterogeneous mixture** consists of substances that are not evenly distributed and have distinct phases.
 
• A **solution** is a **homogeneous mixture**, meaning the solute is uniformly distributed within the solvent.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct related to eco-system?

(i) UV radiation is not damaging to organisms.

(ii) Ozone at the higher levels of the atmosphere is a product of UV radiation acting on oxygen molecule.

(iii) The amount of ozone in the atmosphere began to drop sharply in 1980.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (ii) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **UV radiation** is indeed damaging to organisms as it can cause skin cancer and cataracts in humans, and can also harm marine ecosystems, including phytoplankton.
 
• **Ozone** at the higher levels of the atmosphere (the stratosphere) is indeed a product of UV radiation acting on oxygen molecules (O₂), resulting in the formation of ozone (O₃).
 
• The amount of **ozone** in the atmosphere began to drop sharply in the **1980s** due to the release of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and other ozone-depleting substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UV radiation**__

 __
 
• UV radiation is a form of electromagnetic radiation that comes from the sun and artificial sources like tanning beds.
 
• It has both beneficial and harmful effects. For instance, it helps in the production of vitamin D in humans but excessive exposure can cause skin cancer.
 
 
 
• **Ozone Layer**__
 __
 
• The ozone layer is a region of Earth's stratosphere that absorbs most of the Sun's ultraviolet radiation.
 
• It contains high concentrations of ozone (O₃) molecules.
 
• The ozone layer was significantly depleted by human-made chemicals, primarily CFCs, leading to global environmental issues such as the ozone hole.
 
 
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**__
 
 
• CFCs are compounds that were commonly used in air conditioning, refrigeration, and as propellants in aerosol sprays.
 
• They are harmful to the ozone layer because they release chlorine atoms upon exposure to UV radiation, which then deplete ozone molecules.
 
• The use of CFCs has been largely phased out under the **Montreal Protocol**, an international treaty agreed upon in 1987 to protect the ozone layer.

questions.question: The speed of light is ______.

options.text: greater in water than in air
same in air, glass and water
greater in water than in glass
greater in glass than in water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**greater in water than in glass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **speed of light** varies in different media.
 
• In a vacuum, the speed of light is approximately **299,792 kilometers per second (km/s)**.
 
• When light travels from one medium to another, its speed changes due to the **refractive index** of the media.
 
• The **refractive index of water** is about **1.33**, while the **refractive index of glass** is typically around **1.5**.
 
• A higher refractive index indicates that light travels more slowly in that medium. Therefore, light travels faster in water than in glass.
 
• This is because the **refractive index** of water is lower than that of glass, meaning there is less optical density to slow down the light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **greater in water than in air**__

 __
 
• Light travels slower in water than in air because the **refractive index of air** is approximately **1.0003**, which is lower than that of water.
 
 
 
• **same in air, glass and water**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because the speed of light changes as it moves between different media with different **refractive indices**.
 
 
 
• **greater in glass than in water**__
 
 
• This is incorrect as the **refractive index** of glass is higher than that of water, meaning light travels slower in glass.

questions.question: Which one of the following organisms shows multiple fission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasmodium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plasmodium** is a genus of parasitic protozoa, many of which cause malaria in humans and other animals.
 
• **Multiple fission** is a form of asexual reproduction where a single organism divides into many new organisms simultaneously.
 
• In **Plasmodium**, multiple fission occurs during the **schizogony stage** of its life cycle.
 
• During schizogony, the nucleus of the parasite divides multiple times before the cell splits into several daughter cells called **merozoites**.
 
• This process allows **Plasmodium** to rapidly increase its population within the host, contributing to the spread of malaria.
 
• The life cycle of **Plasmodium** involves both a human host and a mosquito vector (usually of the genus **Anopheles**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydra**__

 __
 
• **Hydra** is a simple freshwater animal of the phylum **Cnidaria**.
 
• It reproduces asexually through a process called **budding**, not multiple fission.
 
• In budding, a new organism grows out of the body of the parent organism.
 
 
 
• **Leishmania**__
 __
 
• **Leishmania** is a genus of trypanosomes that cause the disease **leishmaniasis**.
 
• It reproduces asexually by **binary fission** rather than multiple fission.
 
• Leishmania is transmitted by the bite of infected **sandflies**.
 
 
 
• **Yeast**__
 
 
• **Yeast** is a type of fungus that reproduces asexually primarily through a process called **budding**.
 
• In budding, a new cell grows out from the surface of the parent cell.
 
• Yeast is widely used in the baking and brewing industries due to its ability to ferment sugars.

questions.question: In what duration will a sum of money double itself at 5% per annum simple interest?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
To **double** a sum, the **Interest** must be equal to 100% of the **Principal**.

Time (T) = 100 ÷ Rate %

Time (T) = 100 ÷ 5 = 20 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dbbd3f81e50660584b6672a63831e986e96fb9b0796a36066ebd2b521ad57580.png] 
**Given:**

Let the **Principal (P)** be ₹100.

Since the sum **doubles** itself, the **Amount (A)** = 2 × 100 = ₹200.

**Simple Interest (SI)** = Amount − Principal = 200 − 100 = ₹100.

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ 100 = (100 × 5 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 100 = 5 × T

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 5

⇒ T = 20 years

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Multiplier Rule

If a sum becomes 'n' times in 'T' years, then (n − 1) = (R × T) ÷ 100. For doubling, n = 2.

Rate and Time Relation

Rate and Time are inversely proportional for a fixed interest amount. R = 100(n − 1) ÷ T.

Rule of 72 (CI Approximation)

In Compound Interest, a sum doubles in approximately 72 ÷ R years. For SI, it is exactly 100 ÷ R years.

questions.question: What is the measure of each exterior angle of a regular decagon?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any **regular polygon**, the sum of all **exterior angles** is always 360°.

A **decagon** has **n = 10** sides.

Each exterior angle = 360° ÷ n = 360° ÷ 10 = 36°.

**∴ The correct answer is 36°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Shape = **Regular Decagon**.

**Formula Used:** Each Exterior Angle of a regular polygon = 360° ÷ n, where n is the number of sides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a2b72e1261369c8a63c48343eccdefc3b8f9544fd31dcbe167743db8bd0cdf4.png] 

⇒ Number of sides in a **decagon** (n) = 10.

⇒ Sum of all exterior angles of any **convex polygon** = 360°.

⇒ Since the polygon is **regular**, all exterior angles are equal.

⇒ Each exterior angle = 360° ÷ 10.

⇒ Each exterior angle = 36°.

**∴ The correct answer is 36°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Interior Angle of a Regular Polygon

Each interior angle is given by [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n. For a decagon, it is [(10 − 2) × 180°] ÷ 10 = 144°.

Relation between Interior and Exterior Angles

The sum of an **interior angle** and its corresponding **exterior angle** is always 180° (linear pair).

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of an n-sided polygon is (n − 2) × 180°.</p

questions.question: Which of the following was discovered by Rutherford’s gold foil experiment?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Nucleus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **gold foil experiment** was conducted by **Ernest Rutherford** in 1909.
 
• This experiment involved the **bombardment of gold foil** with alpha particles.
 
• Rutherford observed that most of the alpha particles passed through the foil, but some were **deflected at large angles**.
 
• He concluded that atoms have a **small, dense, positively charged center** which he called the **nucleus**.
 
• Rutherford's findings significantly changed the **atomic model** from J.J. Thomson's plum pudding model to the nuclear model.
 
• The discovery of the nucleus led to a better understanding of the **structure of the atom** and the nature of atomic interactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Neutron**__

 __
 
• The **neutron** was discovered by **James Chadwick** in 1932.
 
• It is a **neutral particle** found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• Neutrons play a crucial role in the **stability of the nucleus**.
 
 
 
• **Electron**__
 __
 
• The **electron** was discovered by **J.J. Thomson** in 1897.
 
• Electrons are **negatively charged particles** that orbit the nucleus of an atom.
 
• They are essential in chemical bonding and electricity.
 
 
 
• **Proton**__
 
 
• The **proton** was discovered by **Ernest Rutherford** in 1917.
 
• Protons are **positively charged particles** found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The number of protons in the nucleus determines the **atomic number** and identity of an element.

questions.question: Which of the following is the general formula of alkane?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Alkanes are a class of **hydrocarbons** that consist of only single bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• The general formula for alkanes is **CnH2n+2**, where **n** represents the number of carbon atoms.
 
• Alkanes are also known as **paraffins** and are saturated hydrocarbons.
 
• They are the simplest type of hydrocarbon and are typically found in **natural gas** and **petroleum**.
 
• Examples of alkanes include **methane (CH4), ethane (C2H6), and propane (C3H8)**.
 
• Alkanes are used as **fuels** and **lubricants** due to their properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **C2nH2n**__

 __
 
• This formula does not correspond to any common class of hydrocarbons.
 
 
 
• **CnHn**__
 __
 
• This formula does not align with any known hydrocarbons.
 
 
 
• **CnH2n**__
 
 
• This formula represents the general formula for **alkenes**, which are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one **carbon-carbon double bond**.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the mixture of air?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Homogeneous mixture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **homogeneous mixture** is a mixture that has the same composition throughout.
 
• In a homogeneous mixture, the different components are uniformly distributed at the molecular level.
 
• Air is a mixture of different gases such as **nitrogen (78%)**, **oxygen (21%)**, and small amounts of other gases like **argon** and **carbon dioxide**.
 
• These gases are thoroughly mixed, resulting in a uniform composition throughout the sample.
 
• Because the composition is uniform, air is considered a homogeneous mixture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Suspension**__

 __
 
• A **suspension** is a heterogeneous mixture in which solid particles are dispersed in a liquid or gas but are not dissolved.
 
• In a suspension, the particles are large enough to eventually settle out due to gravity.
 
• An example of a suspension is muddy water, where soil particles are dispersed in water.
 
 
 
• **Heterogeneous mixture**__
 __
 
• A **heterogeneous mixture** is a mixture where the components are not uniformly distributed, and different parts of the mixture have different compositions.
 
• An example of a heterogeneous mixture is a salad, where different ingredients like lettuce, tomatoes, and cucumbers can be seen and separated physically.
 
 
 
• **Colloids**__
 
 
• A **colloid** is a mixture where very small particles of one substance are evenly distributed throughout another substance.
 
• The particles in a colloid are larger than those in a solution but smaller than those in a suspension.
 
• An example of a colloid is milk, which contains fat droplets dispersed in water.

questions.question: If the earth had no atmosphere, then the colour of the sky would be ______
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**black**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the absence of an atmosphere, the sky would appear **black** instead of its usual blue color.
 
• This is because there would be no air molecules to scatter the sunlight, a phenomenon known as **Rayleigh scattering**.
 
• **Rayleigh scattering** is responsible for scattering shorter wavelengths of light, such as blue, more than longer wavelengths.
 
• The scattered blue light is what makes the sky appear blue to our eyes when the sun is up.
 
• Without an atmosphere, sunlight would travel directly to the surface without scattering, leaving the sky dark and black, similar to how it appears from space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Blue**__

 __
 
• The sky appears **blue** because of the scattering of sunlight by the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• The shorter blue wavelengths are scattered in all directions by the air molecules, making the sky look blue from the ground.
 
 
 
• **Yellow**__
 __
 
• The sky can appear **yellow** during sunrise or sunset due to the scattering of longer wavelengths of light, such as red and yellow.
 
• This occurs when the sun is low on the horizon and the light has to travel through more of the Earth's atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Red**__
 
 
• The sky can appear **red** during sunrise or sunset, similar to yellow, but with even more scattering of shorter wavelengths.
 
• This is often seen when there are particles or pollutants in the air that enhance the scattering effect.

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of 22.5, 56, 42.5, 2x + 1, x - 2, 3x, 36 is 30. Find x, where x > 0
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of 7 numbers = 30 × 7 = 210

Sum of constant terms = 22.5 + 56 + 42.5 + 1 − 2 + 36 = 156

Sum of variables = 2x + x + 3x = 6x

6x + 156 = 210 ⇒ 6x = 54 ⇒ x = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c080f7c1cc9639db67838547ffbef3b2c0feb86689e28e395fae7702f61152fb.png] 

**Given:** Observations = {22.5, 56, 42.5, 2x + 1, x − 2, 3x, 36}, Count (n) = 7, Mean = 30

**Formula Used:** Sum of observations = Mean × Total number of observations

⇒ (22.5 + 56 + 42.5 + 2x + 1 + x − 2 + 3x + 36) = 30 × 7

⇒ (22.5 + 56 + 42.5 + 1 − 2 + 36) + (2x + x + 3x) = 210

⇒ 156 + 6x = 210

⇒ 6x = 210 − 156

⇒ 6x = 54

⇒ x = 54 ÷ 6

⇒ x = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean Properties

If each observation is increased by a constant 'k', the **new mean** also increases by 'k'. If multiplied by 'k', the mean is multiplied by 'k'.

Sum of Deviations

The sum of **deviations** of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. ∑(xᵢ − mean) = 0.

Weighted Average

When observations have different **weights**, the mean is calculated as (∑wᵢxᵢ) ÷ ∑wᵢ.</p

questions.question: The shortest distance measured from the initial to the final position of an object is known as ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**displacement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Displacement** is a vector quantity, which means it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• It measures the shortest distance from the initial to the final position of an object.
 
• Displacement is different from distance, which is a scalar quantity and measures the total path length traveled by an object without considering direction.
 
• It is important in physics because it provides information about the change in position of an object in a specified direction.
 
• Displacement can be positive, negative, or zero, depending on the direction of movement.
 
• In mathematical terms, displacement is often represented as a change in position, denoted as Δx in one-dimensional motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration**__

 __
 
• **Acceleration** is the rate at which an object's velocity changes over time.
 
• It is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.
 
• Acceleration can be caused by changes in speed, direction, or both.
 
 
 
• **Speed**__
 __
 
• **Speed** is a scalar quantity that refers to how fast an object is moving.
 
• It is the rate at which an object covers distance, measured in units such as meters per second (m/s).
 
• Unlike velocity, speed does not consider the direction of movement.
 
 
 
• **Velocity**__
 
 
• **Velocity** is a vector quantity that describes the speed of an object in a particular direction.
 
• It can be represented as the displacement divided by the time taken.
 
• Velocity is important in understanding the motion of objects in physics.

questions.question: When an object moves in a circular path with uniform speed, its motion is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**uniform circular motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object moves in a **circular path** with a **uniform speed**, it is said to be in **uniform circular motion**.
 
• In uniform circular motion, the **speed** of the object remains **constant**, but the **direction** of the velocity changes continuously.
 
• This continuous change in direction means that the object is always undergoing **acceleration**, even though the speed is constant.
 
• The acceleration in uniform circular motion is called **centripetal acceleration**, and it is directed towards the **centre of the circular path**.
 
• Examples of uniform circular motion include the **motion of a satellite orbiting the Earth**, the **rotation of a ceiling fan**, and the **motion of a car turning in a roundabout**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Motion along a hemisphere**__

 __
 
• This refers to the motion of an object along the surface of a **hemisphere**. It is not related to uniform circular motion.
 
• Examples might include the motion of a ball on a dome-shaped surface, but it is not uniform circular motion.
 
 
 
• **Motion along a straight line**__
 __
 
• This is also known as **linear motion** or **rectilinear motion**.
 
• In this type of motion, an object moves in a straight path without changing its direction.
 
• Examples include a car driving on a straight road or a train moving on straight tracks.
 
 
 
• **Linear motion**__
 
 
• This type of motion refers to the movement of an object in a **straight line**.
 
• Linear motion can be uniform (constant speed) or non-uniform (changing speed).
 
• Examples include the motion of a sprinter running on a straight track or an elevator moving up and down.

questions.question: Which of the following endocrine glands secretes growth hormones?

__
 
• The **pituitary gland** is often referred to as the **"master gland"** of the endocrine system.
 
• It is located at the base of the brain, beneath the hypothalamus.
 
• The pituitary gland has two parts: the anterior pituitary and the posterior pituitary, each releasing different hormones.
 
• The anterior pituitary produces and releases **growth hormone (GH)**, which stimulates growth, cell reproduction, and regeneration in humans.
 
• The secretion of growth hormone is regulated by the hypothalamus through releasing and inhibiting hormones.
 
• Growth hormone plays a crucial role in physical development in children and adolescents and also helps maintain tissues and organs throughout life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Thyroid gland**__

 __
 
• The **thyroid gland** is located in the neck and produces hormones like **thyroxine (T4)** and **triiodothyronine (T3)**.
 
• These hormones regulate the body's metabolism, energy levels, and growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Adrenal gland**__
 __
 
• The **adrenal glands** are located on top of each kidney.
 
• They produce hormones such as **adrenaline** (epinephrine), **cortisol**, and aldosterone.
 
• These hormones help regulate metabolism, immune response, and stress responses.
 
 
 
• **Testes**__

questions.question: The energy transfer within the food web has a ______ pattern.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unidirectional**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a food web, the **energy transfer** follows a **unidirectional** pattern.
 
• This means that energy flows in one direction—from the **producers** (such as plants) to various levels of **consumers** (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores).
 
• Producers capture energy from the **sun** through the process of **photosynthesis**.
 
• This captured energy is then transferred to **herbivores** that consume the plants.
 
• From herbivores, the energy is passed on to **carnivores** and **omnivores** that eat the herbivores.
 
• At each transfer, a portion of the energy is **lost as heat**, making the transfer **inefficient** and ensuring that it does not revert back to the previous stage.
 
• The **laws of thermodynamics** support this unidirectional flow, particularly the second law which states that energy transformations are not 100% efficient.
 
• This unidirectional flow helps maintain the **structure** and **function** of ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Circular**__

 __
 
• The term **circular** is not applicable to energy transfer in a food web because energy is not recycled in the same manner as **nutrients** in an ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Multidimensional**__
 __
 
• **Multidimensional** suggests multiple directions or dimensions, which is not accurate for the one-way flow of energy in food webs.
 
 
 
• **Bidirectional**__
 
 
• **Bidirectional** would imply energy flows in two directions, which is not true for food webs as energy moves from producers to consumers in a one-way direction.

questions.question: An object is placed in front of a concave mirror of focal length f, and it is found that an image of the same size as that of the object is formed. The object distance u is:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• For a **concave mirror**, when the object is placed at a distance **equal to the radius of curvature (2f)**, the image formed is of the **same size as that of the object**.
 
• The image formed in this case is **real, inverted**, and of the **same size** as the object.
 
• This is derived from the **mirror formula** and the **magnification** equation for concave mirrors.
 
• According to the **mirror equation**: *1/f = 1/v + 1/u*, where *f* is the focal length, *v* is the image distance, and *u* is the object distance.
 
• For an image to be the same size as the object, the object distance *u* must be **equal to 2f**.
 
• This scenario is a classic case of image formation by concave mirrors used in optics problems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __

• It can form **real and virtual images**, depending on the position of the object.
 
• It is often used in applications like **reflecting telescopes, makeup mirrors**, and **headlights of vehicles**.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length**__
 
 
• The **focal length** (**f**) is the distance between the mirror's surface and the **focal point**.
 
• It is half of the radius of curvature (**R**), i.e., *f = R/2*.
 
• Focal length is a crucial parameter in determining the image formation properties of the mirror.

questions.question: If the price of sugar decreases by 20%, then by what percentage must a householder increase her consumption of sugar so as to leave her expenditure on sugar unchanged?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct formula for **expenditure constant**: % Increase in consumption = [r ÷ (100 − r)] × 100

Here, **r = 20%** (decrease in price).

% Increase = [20 ÷ (100 − 20)] × 100 = (20 ÷ 80) × 100 = (1/4) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Decrease in **price of sugar** = 20%. Expenditure remains **unchanged**.

**Formula:** Expenditure = Price × Consumption

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a036b1495a0d098e4050d0641d4af3467ff378fa9a228a552a749b35d303779b.png] 

⇒ Let original **Price** = 100 and original **Consumption** = 100.

⇒ Original **Expenditure** = 100 × 100 = 10,000.

⇒ New **Price** = 100 − 20% of 100 = 80.

⇒ Since Expenditure is unchanged, New Consumption = 10,000 ÷ 80 = 125.

⇒ Increase in **Consumption** = 125 − 100 = 25.

⇒ % Increase = (25 ÷ 100) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Variation Rule

When the product of two variables is **constant** (Price × Consumption = Expenditure), an x% decrease in one requires a [x ÷ (100 − x)] × 100% increase in the other.

Percentage Change in Expenditure

If both price and consumption change, the net % change in expenditure is given by the **successive percentage formula**: a + b + (ab/100).

Fractional Conversion

A 20% decrease is a factor of 1/5. To keep the product same, consumption must increase by 1/(5−1) = 1/4, which is **25%**.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper lists the price of a fan at 22% above its cost price and offers a 15% discount on its list price. What is the cost price (in Rs. ) of the fan if he sells it at Rs. 5,185?

questions.question: Lakhan and Ram start a business by investing Rs. 48,000 and Rs. 72,000, respectively. What is Ram’s share out of the annual profit of Rs. 6,530?

Investment ratio of **Lakhan** and **Ram** = 48,000 : 72,000 = 2 : 3.

Total ratio parts = 2 + 3 = 5 units.

Total annual profit = Rs. 6,530.

Value of 1 unit = 6,530 ÷ 5 = Rs. 1,306.

Ram's share (3 units) = 3 × 1,306 = Rs. 3,918.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,918.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be6f5520c743cc4d431a74a449ad369e1d5b047cfe7b7beb738868103e320ac0.png]

Partnership Basics

Compound Partnership

questions.question: There are two classrooms A and B having a certain number of students. If 5 students are shifted from A to B, then B has twice the number of students as A. If 1 student is sent from B to A, then both classrooms will have the same number of students. How many students are there in B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the number of students in **Class A** be A and **Class B** be B.

From the second condition: If 1 student goes from B to A, they become equal ⇒ **B − 1 = A + 1** ⇒ **B − A = 2**.

Check options for **B**: If B = 19, then A = 17.

Verify first condition: If 5 shift from A to B, A becomes 17 − 5 = 12, and B becomes 19 + 5 = 24.

Since 24 is **twice** of 12, the condition is satisfied.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8ac63ce07f1385157e7438216d31e6a2a4c99e54ff28cb8af9e4b6fac26e3588.png] 

Let **Class A** have x students and **Class B** have y students.

**Case 1:** 5 students shifted from A to B.

⇒ 2(x − 5) = y + 5

⇒ 2x − 10 = y + 5 ⇒ 2x − y = 15 --- (Eq. 1)

**Case 2:** 1 student sent from B to A.

⇒ x + 1 = y − 1

⇒ y − x = 2 ⇒ x = y − 2 --- (Eq. 2)

Substitute x in Eq. 1:

⇒ 2(y − 2) − y = 15

⇒ 2y − 4 − y = 15

⇒ y = 19

**∴ The correct answer is 19 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Substitution Method

Expressing one variable in terms of the other from the **simpler equation** and substituting it into the more complex one to find the value.

Elimination Method

Multiplying equations by suitable constants so that adding or subtracting them **eliminates one variable**.</p

questions.question: The number of factors of any prime number is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

By the fundamental definition of **number systems**, a **prime number** is a natural number greater than **1** that cannot be formed by multiplying two smaller natural numbers.

This implies that it is divisible only by **1** and the **number itself**.

Therefore, the set of factors for any prime number **p** is strictly **{1, p}**.

The total count of these factors is always exactly **2**.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A **prime number**.

**Definition:** A prime number is a **positive integer** that has no positive divisors other than **1** and **itself**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c7717892329d7d28cc5171472d81126e4cb96185085668ef3a33bf675ef74916.png] 

⇒ Let us verify with examples:

⇒ For **2** (smallest prime): Factors are 1 and 2. Count = **2**.

⇒ For **3**: Factors are 1 and 3. Count = **2**.

⇒ For **11**: Factors are 1 and 11. Count = **2**.

⇒ For **19**: Factors are 1 and 19. Count = **2**.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Composite Numbers

Natural numbers that have more than **two factors** (e.g., 4 has factors 1, 2, and 4).

Special Case of 1

The number **1** has only one factor (itself), so it is **neither prime nor composite**.

Even Prime Number

The number **2** is the only **even** prime number; all other prime numbers are odd.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be **co-prime** if their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is 1.</p

questions.question: The ratio between the present ages of Amit and Amita is 7 : 5, respectively. The ratio between Amit’s age 5 years ago and Amita’s age 5 years hence is 1 : 1. After how many years from now will the age of Amit and Amita together be 72 years?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Ratio of present ages of **Amit** and **Amita** = 7 : 5.

Ratio (Amit − 5) : (Amita + 5) = 1 : 1 ⇒ Amit − 5 = Amita + 5 ⇒ Amit − Amita = 10 years.

Difference in ratio parts (7 − 5) = 2 units. So, 2 units = 10 years ⇒ 1 unit = 5 years.

Present sum of ages = (7 + 5) × 5 = 60 years. Target sum = 72 years.

Total years to add = 72 − 60 = 12 years. Since there are 2 people, each grows by 12 ÷ 2 = 6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Present age ratio = 7 : 5. Condition: (Amit − 5)/(Amita + 5) = 1/1.

**Formula Used:** Age after n years = Present Age + n.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a9906182df9ee893ab79e7d37a3b41609d9aeb8f2cd1d38d9df77be82817dab.png] 
⇒ Let **Amit** present age = 7x and **Amita** present age = 5x.

⇒ According to the question: (7x − 5) / (5x + 5) = 1 / 1

⇒ 7x − 5 = 5x + 5

⇒ 2x = 10 ⇒ x = 5.

⇒ Amit present age = 7 × 5 = 35 years; Amita present age = 5 × 5 = 25 years.

⇒ Total present age = 35 + 25 = 60 years.

⇒ Let after 'n' years their total age be 72.

⇒ (35 + n) + (25 + n) = 72

⇒ 60 + 2n = 72 ⇒ 2n = 12 ⇒ n = 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Concept of Constant Difference

The difference between the ages of two people always remains constant, regardless of the number of years passed or subtracted.

Ratio and Proportions in Ages

When a ratio a:b is given for present ages, we use a common variable 'x' to represent actual values as ax and bx. For 'n' years later, we use (ax+n) and (bx+n).

Total Sum of Ages

If the sum of ages of 'k' people is 'S' now, then after 'n' years, the total sum will be S + (k × n).</p

questions.question: Aman sells two houses at the rate of Rs. 1.995 lakhs each. On one he gains 5% and on the other he loses 5%. His gain or loss percentage in the whole transaction is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two items are sold at the **same Selling Price (SP)**, one at a **gain of x%** and another at a **loss of x%**, there is always a **net loss**.

Shortcut: **Net Loss% = x² ÷ 100**.

Given x = 5.

Net Loss% = 5² ÷ 100 = 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.25% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP of each house = **Rs. 1.995 lakhs**, Gain = 5%, Loss = 5%.

**Formulas:** CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 ± Profit/Loss%), Net Loss% = (x² ÷ 100)%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c17dabf2b34055eeca49eec924a2d0bc155793ad713045d29baab1f6c51c8c51.png] 

⇒ House 1 CP = 1.995 × 100 ÷ 105 = 1.9 lakhs.

⇒ House 2 CP = 1.995 × 100 ÷ 95 = 2.1 lakhs.

⇒ Total CP = 1.9 + 2.1 = 4.0 lakhs.

⇒ Total SP = 1.995 × 2 = 3.99 lakhs.

⇒ Net Loss = 4.0 − 3.99 = 0.01 lakh.

⇒ Net Loss% = (0.01 ÷ 4.0) × 100 = 0.25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.25% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Two same-SP articles

If two articles are sold at the same price, one at x% profit and another at x% loss, the transaction always results in a **loss** of **(x/10)²%**.

Successive Percentage Change

The net change can also be calculated using the formula **a + b + (ab/100)**, where a is +5 and b is −5.</p

questions.question: A book is pushed with a constant force of 1 N. It displaces 1 m in the direction of the force. The work done by the force is:
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Work Done** is defined as the product of the force applied and the displacement in the direction of the force.
 
• The formula for work done is **W = F × d**, where **W** is the work done, **F** is the force, and **d** is the displacement.
 
• In this case, the force **(F)** is **1 N** and the displacement **(d)** is **1 m**.
 
• Therefore, the work done **(W)** is **1 N × 1 m = 1 J**.
 
• The **positive sign** indicates that the force and the displacement are in the same direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• **Negative work** occurs when the force and the displacement are in opposite directions.
 
• In such cases, the work done is calculated as **-F × d**.
 
• This situation typically occurs in scenarios involving friction or opposing forces.
 
 
 
• **Zero Work Done**__
 
 
• **Zero work** is done when either the force is zero, or the displacement is zero, or the force is perpendicular to the direction of displacement.
 
• In mathematical terms, this can be expressed as **W = 0**.

questions.question: Find the compound interest on Rs. 12,000 in 3 years at a rate of 10% per annum, compounded annually.

For a **3-year period** at **10%**, the **Effective Percentage Rate** of **Compound Interest** is **33.1%**.

Compound Interest = **Principal** × **33.1%**

⇒ 12,000 × 0.331 = 3,972

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3972.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = **Rs. 12,000**, Time (n) = **3 years**, Rate (R) = **10% p.a.**

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ and Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b1c3273ad59eace7eea8d067f50e81bdfa4a41115f0c5959884b9e7386944fdb.png] 

⇒ A = 12000 × (1 + 10/100)³

⇒ A = 12000 × (11/10) × (11/10) × (11/10)

⇒ A = 12 × 11 × 11 × 11

⇒ A = 12 × 1331 = 15,972

⇒ CI = 15,972 − 12,000

⇒ CI = 3,972

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3972.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Interest

For 2 years, effective rate = x + y + (xy/100). For 3 years at 10%, it is 33.1%.

Difference between CI and SI

For 3 years, Difference = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Compound Interest Formula

CI = P[(1 + R/100)ⁿ − 1] where P is principal, R is rate, and n is time.</p

questions.question: If a constant force of 2 Newton is applied on a body such that displacement of the body in the direction of the applied force is zero, then the work done by the force is _______.

__
 
• The **work done** by a force is defined as the product of the force and the **displacement** of the object in the direction of the force.
 
• The formula for work done is: **Work = Force × Displacement × cos(θ)**, where θ is the angle between the force and the direction of displacement.
 
• If the **displacement** of the body is zero, then the work done by any force, regardless of its magnitude, will be **zero**.
 
• In this scenario, the force applied is **2 Newtons**, but the displacement in the direction of the applied force is **zero**.
 
• Therefore, the work done by the force is **0 joules**.
 
• This concept is important in understanding the relationship between force, displacement, and work in the context of **physics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Force**__

 __
 
• A **force** is a push or pull upon an object resulting from the object's interaction with another object.
 
• Forces can cause an object to accelerate, slow down, remain in place, or change shape.
 
• Forces are measured in **Newtons (N)** in the International System of Units (SI).
 
 
 
• **Displacement**__
 __
 
• **Displacement** is a vector quantity that refers to an object's change in position.
 
• It is the shortest distance from the initial to the final position of a point.
 
• Displacement has both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
 
 
• **Work**__
 
 
• **Work** is done when a force causes a displacement of an object.

• Positive work is done when the force and displacement are in the same direction, while negative work is done when they are in opposite directions.

questions.question: The ratio of the volumes of two cubes is 729 : 1331. What is the ratio of their total surface areas?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Volumes** (V₁ : V₂) = 729 : 1331

Ratio of **Sides** (s₁ : s₂) = √³729 : √³1331 = 9 : 11

Ratio of **Surface Areas** (A₁ : A₂) = (s₁)² : (s₂)² = 9² : 11² = 81 : 121

**∴ The correct answer is 81 : 121.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of volumes of two cubes = 729 : 1331

**Formula Used:** Volume of cube = (side)³; Total Surface Area = 6 × (side)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d265dcd55f1ba3588247af0b80c79eef1a094a8d26a6f855a2b3d6d4eec00b8c.png]

⇒ a₁ / a₂ = √³(729 / 1331) = 9 / 11

⇒ Ratio of Total Surface Areas = (6 × a₁²) / (6 × a₂²)

⇒ Ratio = (a₁ / a₂)² = (9 / 11)²

⇒ Ratio = 81 / 121

**∴ The correct answer is 81 : 121.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cube Properties

For a cube of side 'a', the **Diagonal** is a√3 and the **Lateral Surface Area** is 4a².

Scaling Rules

If the ratio of sides of two similar figures is x : y, then the ratio of their **areas** is x² : y² and the ratio of their **volumes** is x³ : y³.</p

questions.question: An organism simply splits into two equal halves during cell division. What is it known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Binary fission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Binary fission** is a form of asexual reproduction.
 
• In this process, a single organism divides into two equal parts.
 
• Each part develops into a new organism identical to the parent.
 
• This method is common in **prokaryotic organisms** like bacteria.
 
• It ensures rapid population growth in favorable environments.
 
• **Binary fission** occurs through simple mitotic cell division.
 
• Examples of organisms that reproduce by binary fission include **Amoeba and Paramecium**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Regeneration**__

 __
 
• **Regeneration** is the process by which organisms replace or restore lost or damaged tissues or body parts.
 
• It is seen in organisms like **starfish, lizards, and planarians**.
 
• Unlike binary fission, regeneration involves the formation of new tissues from the remaining part.
 
 
 
• **Spore formation**__
 __
 
• **Spore formation** is a method of asexual reproduction where an organism produces spores that develop into new individuals.
 
• This method is common in **fungi, algae, and some bacteria**.
 
• Spores are typically resistant to harsh environmental conditions.
 
 
 
• **Budding**__
 
 
• **Budding** is an asexual reproduction method where a new organism grows from a bud on the parent organism.
 
• It is observed in organisms like **yeasts and hydras**.
 
• The new organism remains attached until it is mature and then detaches.

questions.question: If A’s income is 40% less than B’s income, then A's income is what percentage of B's income?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **B's income** = 100.

**A's income** is 40% less → 100 − 40 = 60.

Percentage of **A's income** with respect to **B's income** = (60 ÷ 100) × 100 = 60%.

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage reduction = 40%

**Formula Used:**

A's Income = B's Income × (100 − Reduction%) ÷ 100

Required Percentage = (A's Income ÷ B's Income) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **B's income** = 100 units

⇒ **A's income** = 100 − 40% of 100

⇒ **A's income** = 100 − 40 = 60 units

⇒ Required Percentage = (60 ÷ 100) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Comparison

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by x% and then by y%, the **net effective change** is given by [x + y + (xy ÷ 100)]%.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

Common fractions help in **fast calculations**: 1/5 = 20%, 2/5 = 40%, 3/5 = 60%, and 4/5 = 80%.</p

questions.question: An object is placed between F and 2F of a concave lens. Which of the following options represents the characteristics of the image formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virtual and diminished**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave lens** is also known as a **diverging lens** because it spreads out light rays that have been refracted through it.
 
• When an object is placed between **F (focus) and 2F** of a concave lens, the image formed is always **virtual**, meaning it cannot be projected on a screen.
 
• The image formed by a concave lens is also **diminished** or smaller in size compared to the object.
 
• The image is formed on the **same side of the lens** as the object.
 
• Such images are also **upright** or erect, as opposed to inverted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Real and enlarged**__

 __
 
• Real images are formed when light rays actually converge at a point. However, concave lenses can never form real images; they always produce virtual images.
 
• Enlarged images are produced by convex lenses when the object is placed between the lens and its focus.
 
 
 
• **Real and diminished**__
 __
 
• Real and diminished images are typically formed by convex lenses when the object is placed beyond 2F.
 
• Concave lenses do not form real images.
 
 
 
• **Virtual and enlarged**__
 
 
• Virtual and enlarged images can be formed by convex lenses when the object is placed between the lens and its focus.
 
• Concave lenses, however, always form diminished images.

questions.question: A current of 1 A is drawn by a filament of an electric bulb for 5 minutes. Then the amount of electric charge that flows through the circuit will be _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**300 C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The amount of **electric charge** that flows through a circuit is calculated using the formula: **Q = I × t**, where **Q** is the charge, **I** is the current, and **t** is the time.
 
• Here, the **current (I)** is given as **1 A** (ampere).
 
• The **time (t)** is given as **5 minutes**. Since the standard unit of time in this formula is seconds, we need to convert minutes to seconds: **5 minutes = 5 × 60 = 300 seconds**.
 
• Using the formula: **Q = I × t = 1 A × 300 s = 300 C** (coulombs).
 
• Hence, the amount of electric charge that flows through the circuit is **300 C**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Current (I)**__

 __
 
• The **electric current** is the flow of electric charge in a circuit.
 
• It is measured in **amperes (A)**.
 
• One **ampere** is equal to one coulomb of charge passing through a point in a circuit per second.
 
 
 
• **Time (t)**__
 __
 
• The **time** in this context is the duration for which the current flows.
 
• It is measured in **seconds (s)** in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• When given in minutes, it should be converted to seconds for calculations involving electric charge and current.
 
 
 
• **Electric Charge (Q)**__
 
 
• The **electric charge** is the amount of electricity transported by a current.
 
• It is measured in **coulombs (C)**.
 
• One **coulomb** is equivalent to the charge transferred by a one-ampere current in one second.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a suitable method to deal with non-biodegradable substances?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Throw them openly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-biodegradable substances** are materials that do not decompose or take an extremely long time to break down naturally.
 
• These substances, if not managed properly, can cause significant **environmental pollution** and harm to **wildlife** and human health.
 
• Throwing them openly leads to **land pollution**, **water contamination**, and potential harm to living organisms.
 
• It is crucial to manage non-biodegradable waste responsibly to maintain a sustainable and healthy environment.

• **Reusing** non-biodegradable items reduces the demand for new products and minimizes waste.
 
• This method can include using items multiple times or repurposing them for other uses.
 
 
 
• **Recycle them**__
 __
 
• **Recycling** involves processing used materials into new products, conserving resources, and reducing landfill waste.
 
• Common recyclable materials include **plastics, metals, glass, and paper.**
 
 
 
• **Reduce their production**__
 
 
• Reducing the production of non-biodegradable substances helps to lower the overall environmental impact.
 
• This can be achieved through innovation in product design and encouraging sustainable consumption practices.
